{"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the upper tail of the fish (stroke 3), the whole upper fork from the top body line round the tip toward the notch. The tail is what makes the outline read as a fish rather than a blob, so it was a key piece of the picture. Before the push, the full run was dark from the nose, with all 118 dominoes connected to the start.

Execution: I took stroke 3 as soon as it was assigned and traced it steadily in small batches from about 1:45 to 5:15. I waited until the top body run was connected through before carrying on, which avoided wasted work. I kept the tip soft and curved, as the sharp-corner rule requires, and ended it close to the other line without forcing a join at the notch. When it was done I inspected the notch area to confirm the fall still carried through. After that I kept my hands off the structure so nothing got bumped before the push.

Collaboration: I gave the table regular, short status updates on how far the upper tail had got and when it would be finished, so the others could time their checks of the fork. I followed Sofia's and Hana's advice not to join at the notch, which kept that stretch simple and reliable. I kept the mood light with the team as the clock ran down.

Leadership: I led by reliability and communication in my own piece. I said what I was doing, gave honest progress, and called when it was done. I helped keep the table calm and focused through the final minutes, and I backed the group's decision to stop touching the structure once it was fully connected. I think my share of the result was about a quarter, centred on the upper tail and the check of the notch.", "my_share_percent": 27}
